\[

&\Delta=e^{-t_{s} / \tau} \\

\end{aligned}

Combine the exponents:

\[

\]

Integrate \( e^{-(s + a) t} \) with respect to \( t \):

\[
Y(s) = \left[ \frac{-1}{s + a} e^{-(s + a) t} \right]_{0}^{\infty}
\]

Evaluate the limits:

- At \( t \to \infty \), \( e^{-(s + a) t} \to 0 \) (assuming \( \text{Re}(s) > -a \)).
- At \( t = 0 \), \( e^{-(s + a) \cdot 0} = 1 \).

Thus:

\[
Y(s) = \left[ 0 - \left( \frac{-1}{s + a} \cdot 1 \right) \right] = \frac{1}{s + a}
\]
